prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one polished, highly legible portrait-tablet application screenshot (900x1200) for MI Drug Test, matching the restrained white, Geist-like typography, blue actions, thin gray borders and compact cards of the reference images. The references are style references, not edit targets. Use Payload's existing header with hamburger, home icon and breadcrumb "Lab results"; do not draw a customized sidebar. This is a proposed SINGLE workflow for entering either a lab screening report or a confirmation report. Top 4-step progress: Upload (complete), Match (active blue), Results, Review. Page title "Match lab report". File row "lab-results.pdf" with small amber badge "Screen + confirmation" and link "Review PDF", plus unobtrusive "Change report" action. One compact client identity card with SAME fictional male headshot style and text "Alex Morgan", "DOB Jan 14, 1990", tiny Edit action. Below a single compact card titled "Choose the collection" containing two radio-selectable rows for the SAME client: "11-Panel Lab · Oct 3, 2026 · 10:30 AM" with amber status "Awaiting confirmation" selected, and "11-Panel Lab · Sep 18, 2026 · 9:00 AM" with gray status "Final". This demonstrates matching a specific COLLECTION, not only donor identity. No account IDs. No duplicated client names or DOB in the collection rows. No medications on this step. Bottom navigation: outlined Back left, primary "Continue to results" right. Realistic web UI, short text only, ample but compact spacing. No paragraph explaining parsing, no analytics, no confidence percentages, no extra confirmation checkbox for exact match, no decorative medical illustrations. Keep each label clearly readable. Detection badge is informational; changing report type can be placed in an unexpanded "Report options" accordion.

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one polished, highly legible portrait-tablet application screenshot (900x1200) for MI Drug Test, closely matching the white, Geist-like typography, blue buttons, thin gray borders and compact card style of the supplied references. References are style references only. Payload built-in top header with hamburger and breadcrumb "Lab results"; no custom sidebar. 4-step progress: Upload checked, Match checked, Results active blue, Review gray. Title "Review lab results". Compact identity card with fictional male headshot "Alex Morgan", "DOB Jan 14, 1990 · 11-Panel Lab", small "Edit" link. One single main results card: small badge "Screening report" and "Review PDF" link in its header, compact red strip with icon and text "Unexpected positive: THC"; immediately below "Expected: Buprenorphine · Detected: Buprenorphine, THC". One short medications line "Medication: Suboxone → Buprenorphine" INSIDE THIS CARD, no separate medication card and no medication pictures. Under results, concise heading "Result decision" and three simple radio options: "Accept result", "Request confirmation" selected blue, "Decide later". When confirmation is selected, one concise row "Confirm: THC" with small Change link. No explanation paragraphs. Below, one closed accordion "Edit test details", hiding date, specimen validity and result edits by default. Do not display the same substances in a second large table, no duplicated identity or results panels. Fixed/simple footer: Back on left, blue "Continue to review" on right. Keep practical tablet touch targets, small balanced typography consistent between sections. No ornamental graphics, no colored whole-page backgrounds, no account IDs or payment components.

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one polished, highly legible portrait-tablet application screenshot (900x1200) for MI Drug Test, matching the minimal white, Geist-like typography, blue actions, thin gray borders and compact cards in the references. References are style references only. Payload native top header with hamburger and breadcrumb "Lab results"; no customized sidebar. Four-step progress: Upload checked, Match checked, Results active blue, Review gray. Title "Review lab results". Same compact identity card and fictional male headshot: "Alex Morgan", "DOB Jan 14, 1990 · 11-Panel Lab", small Edit link. ONE results card with header label "Confirmation report" and Review PDF link. Red compact status strip "Unexpected positive: THC". One short line "Medication: Suboxone → Buprenorphine". Then a compact THREE-COLUMN table with clear headers "Substance", "Confirmation", "Measured". First row "THC", red chip "Positive", "85 ng/mL"; second row "Buprenorphine", green-neutral expected chip "Expected", "14 ng/mL"; third row "Fentanyl", yellow chip "Check result", "Not read". The last ambiguous row must be clearly identifiable: only this row has a pale amber background and a small actionable "Review" button or link alongside Check result. It is unknown, do NOT label it negative or show a checked confirmation. Keep analyte/metabolite details behind a closed per-row chevron or small "Analytes" disclosure, not a second duplicated table. One brief helper under table "Review Fentanyl in the PDF." No long warning. Closed "Edit test details" accordion beneath main card. Footer Back left and DISABLED pale blue "Continue to review" right until the unknown result is reviewed. Simple, useful technician UI, no account IDs, no repeated large summary blocks, no payment widgets, no medication pictures or lengthy technical explanation. Visually distinguish expected positive, unexpected positive and unverified extraction without color alone.
